question: Assume today is 2026-10-28. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of UK residential property transactions (with a value of £40,000 or above) in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as it will be first reported (provisional estimate) in HM Revenue & Customs' monthly release 'Monthly property transactions completed in the UK with value of £40,000 or above'.

target.what: Number of completed UK residential property transactions with a value of £40,000 or above in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as first reported as a provisional estimate by HMRC.
target.caveats: Target is completed residential transactions, not sales agreed, listings, or mortgage approvals. Coverage is UK residential only and excludes non-residential property; value threshold is £40,000 or above. Series is seasonally adjusted and the first provisional estimate is subject to later revision d

candidates.hypothesis: Past HMRC seasonally adjusted residential transaction counts, especially August 2026 and the September seasonal pattern from earlier years, plus typical first-provisional-to-revised revisions, provide the primary level and seasonal anchor for September 2026. Recent momentum and SA factors should predict the first provisional print with small revision bias.
candidates.data_to_find: HMRC monthly UK residential property transactions with value >=£40,000, seasonally adjusted, monthly observations through August 2026 and the same month in 2023-2025; first provisional vs later revised values for recent months; HMRC seasonal adjustment methodology/factors. Substitute: UK property transactions all-property series if the residential component is only available separately.
search_hints: HMRC monthly property transactions residential seasonally adjusted August 2026
site:gov.uk property transactions statistics monthly table residential
HMRC property transactions provisional revised seasonal adjustment

candidates.perspective: Bank of England monetary statistics analyst
candidates.hypothesis: UK mortgage approvals for house purchase are a leading indicator of completed residential transactions. September 2026 HMRC transactions should be approximated by lagged BoE approvals (roughly 1-3 months) multiplied by a gross-up/conversion factor covering cash buyers, non-mortgage transfers, approvals that do not complete, and coverage differences. The factor can be estimated from historical aligned series.
candidates.data_to_find: Bank of England monthly UK mortgage approvals for house purchase, seasonally adjusted, Jan-Aug 2026 and longer history; aligned HMRC residential transactions history to estimate lag and approvals-to-transactions ratio; share of cash/non-mortgage residential transactions. Substitute: UK Finance mortgage completions if BoE approvals unavailable.

Deviations from this baseline signal cyclical momentum.

assessment.note: These all report the same HMRC August 2026 release: SA residential transactions 95,220, July 96,650, NSA August 96,250. Multiple media URLs repeat one underlying HMRC measurement, so they are not independent confirmation.

Several media summaries give July 2026 SA transactions as 96,710, while the HMRC release cited in p2/p49 gives 96,650. The July level is a minor transcription/vintage conflict; use the official HMRC figure.
Historical HMRC August SA residential transaction levels, mostly duplicated across releases/media. They establish the sparse August own-history used for momentum, but are not independent of HMRC.

September 2025 first-provisional SA was 95,980 in p39; a later article p92 reports 96,730 for September 2025 after revision. This is a vintage difference, not a real contradiction. For a first-provisional target, p39 is the vintage-aligned anchor; p92 shows revision risk.
Bank of England net house-purchase approvals: August 2026 54,900, July 55,900, six-month average 60,100. These are the authoritative approvals series and show weakening mortgage demand.

Credit Canary gives July approvals as 56,100 while BoE p100 gives 55,900; June 58,200 appears only in the secondary source. Use official July p100 and use June p176 only with caution as a lagged proxy.

Several independent market trackers report sales agreed down roughly 6–9% year-on-year in mid/late 2026 and weak demand, consistent with transaction momentum below normal. These are qualitative demand indicators, not direct HMRC counts.

RICS surveys show September 2026 buyer enquiries and agreed sales weaker than August. For September completions, the more relevant RICS signal is the low April 2026 sales-agreed balance (p403/p496/p585) because completions lag sales agreed by several months.
Bank Rate was held at 3.75% on 17 September 2026. These are consistent reports of the same MPC decision.

Mortgage-rate reports differ by source/date (about 5.5–6.0%), but all point to elevated rates and a housing-demand headwind through September/October 2026. Differences are timing and product-mix rather than contradictions.
TwentyEA/TwentyCi revised the 2026 transaction forecast down to 1.13 million. p345 labels it UK and p360 England and Wales, so scope is ambiguous; use p345 only with a coverage/forecast-error factor.

Several turnover indicators imply roughly 4–5% annual housing turnover or about one move every 20–23 years. p446 gives 29 million UK homes. These provide a slow structural baseline, not a current monthly count.

p81/p408 approximately 40% of transactions are cash sales by count, while the older IMLA figures are value shares (58.3% cash/equity by value in 2014). They are not directly comparable; only the count share belongs in an approvals gross-up.

These duplicate RICS September 2026 results but are marked live/dated 2026-01-01, which is before the reported period and impossible for a September 2026 survey. Discard these copies and use the valid RICS reports.

methods.rationale: Primary own-history route. Uses the latest HMRC SA levels (Aug 2026 p1, Jul 2026 p2, earlier 2026 months), the first-provisional September 2025 anchor p39, and historical August levels for a sparse monthly pattern. The method should extrapolate last year's September first-provisional print by recent year-on-year momentum. Main risks: very short consecutive monthly history, revision differences between first and later vintages, and September-specific seasonal adjustment changes.

p176.role: Net mortgage approvals for house purchase, UK, seasonally adjusted, June 2026, used as about a three-month lead into September 2026 completions

p100.role: Net mortgage approvals for house purchase, UK, seasonally adjusted, July 2026, used as about a two-month lead into September 2026 completions

p81.role: Approximate share of UK residential property transactions that are cash sales, used to gross mortgage-financed completions to all transactions

a1.role: Completion/conversion rate from net house-purchase mortgage approvals to completed HMRC residential transactions by September 2026

methods.rationale: Approvals-to-completions route. Averages June and July 2026 approvals to reflect the stated 2–4 month offer-to-completion lag, converts approvals to mortgage-financed completions via a1, then grosses up for roughly 40% cash sales using p81. Shared dependency: p81 is a count share and a1 is uncertain; both affect the level linearly. Main failure modes: approvals timing, cash-share scope, and approval-to-completion conversion.

p345.role: TwentyEA revised forecast of UK residential property transactions for calendar year 2026

a2.role: September 2026 seasonally adjusted HMRC transaction level as a factor of the annual-forecast monthly average and coverage adjustment

methods.rationale: Annual-forecast constraint route. Takes the revised 2026 annual transaction forecast and spreads it across 12 months, then adjusts for September being close to the seasonally adjusted annual average and for possible forecast scope error. This route is independent of the short HMRC monthly history but depends on a mid-2026 industry forecast; it would fail if the forecast's UK/England-and-Wales scope is misread or if late-2026 momentum is far from the annual average.

p446.role: UK total dwelling stock, approximately 29 million homes

p430.role: Average years between a home changing hands in the UK, used to convert dwelling stock into an annual transaction turnover baseline

a3.role: 2026 current turnover adjustment relative to the 2015 structural norm and HMRC >=£40k residential coverage

methods.rationale: Structural capacity/turnover baseline. Multiplies the UK dwelling stock by an implied turnover rate from the average years between transactions, divides to a monthly figure, and adjusts for the weaker 2026 market versus the older structural norm. This is slow-moving and cannot capture September-specific momentum, so it is a cross-check rather than a primary nowcast. Main risks: p430 is a 2015 vintage, p446 is UK stock, and the current-cycle adjustment a3 is uncertain.

assumptions.name: Share of net house-purchase mortgage approvals completing as HMRC residential transactions by September 2026
assumptions.rationale: Net approvals are already net of cancellations, and most approved house purchases proceed. With roughly 40% cash sales by count (p81), HMRC transactions are substantially larger than mortgage approvals; aligned 2026 HMRC/approvals levels imply a high approval-to-completion rate near 0.98. Some fall-through and timing slippage justify a lower tail.
assumptions.applies_when: June and July 2026 net house-purchase approvals are reasonable lagged proxies for September 2026 completions, and p81 is a transaction-count cash share rather than a value share.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of materially higher approval fall-through, a cash share far from 40% by transaction count, or a completion lag outside 2–4 months.

assumptions.name: September 2026 seasonally adjusted level as a factor of the 2026 annual-forecast monthly average
assumptions.rationale: p345 is a revised 2026 annual transaction forecast. Because the target is seasonally adjusted, September should be close to the annual monthly average, but forecast error and possible UK versus England-and-Wales scope ambiguity require a wide factor.
assumptions.applies_when: p345 is a forecast of UK residential transaction volume comparable to HMRC's >=£40k residential count, and the 2026 forecast remains approximately valid for September.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that p345 covers only England and Wales, that the forecast was materially revised before September, or that September 2026 is far from the annual average on a seasonally adjusted basis.

assumptions.name: 2026 current turnover adjustment relative to the 2015 structural years-between-transactions norm
assumptions.rationale: p446 and p430 imply a long-run turnover baseline. Current conditions are weaker: mortgage rates are elevated, approvals are reported 16% below the 2017–19 average (p404), and sales agreed are down year-on-year (p73/p74). This supports turnover below the old 23-year norm, but cash buyers and regional differences create wide uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: p430/p446 give a usable UK structural turnover baseline and the 2026 market is still below that long-run norm.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that 2026 turnover has returned to or exceeded the 2015 norm, or that p430/p446 are not comparable to HMRC residential transaction counts.

assessment.note: All are the same HMRC August 2026 provisional SA print (95,220) repeated by different outlets; one underlying measurement, not 13 independent confirmations. It is the latest observed level of the target series.

July 2026 SA level. Nine copies give the value as printed in the 30 Sep 2026 release (96,650); p813/p843 give the earlier 3 Sep 2026 vintage (96,710). Same month, two vintages: the revision is only -60 (-0.06%), evidence that first-provisional to next-vintage revisions of this series are small. Only the current vintage (96,650) is used in any series.

2025 anchors on the target definition: Aug 2025 SA 97,040, Jul 2025 SA 97,820, Sep 2025 SA 95,980 (non-SA 102,420). p93/p94 (Oct 2025 release) quote September 2025 as 96,730, i.e. the first provisional September value was later revised UP by ~0.8%; this is the one concrete indication that a first September print can sit slightly below the settled level, but it is a single observation.

Fiscal year-to-date April-August SA: 488,540 (2026) vs 438,800 (2025), +11.3% YoY, which is incompatible with the -2% YoY recorded for August alone. Consistent only if activity in Feb-Apr 2026 (p269, p268, p254) was boosted by the 1 April 2025 SDLT change and the tail-off; so the YTD total cannot be read as a September run-rate without recognising the front-loaded spring.

BoE net house-purchase approvals: 55,900 (Jul), 54,900 (Aug), 6-month average 60,100. Same release repeated across outlets; approvals are falling and stand ~16% below the 2017-19 average, i.e. a headwind for completions around September-December 2026.

Approvals path through 2026: 62,700 (Feb), 63,500 first / 64,000 revised (Mar), 65,900 (Apr), 58,200 (Jun), 55,900 (Jul), 54,900 (Aug). Shows both the level and the vintage-revision pattern (small, +500) and makes clear that the approvals feeding September completions are materially lower than those feeding April-June completions.

HM Land Registry 'transactions for value' rose from 95,818 (Jun) to 103,398 (Jul) 2026, while HMRC SA completions fell from 98,390 (Jun vintage) to 96,650/96,710 (Jul). Different measures (HMLR processing counts, includes non-residential, registration timing), so this is a direction-of-travel warning rather than a contradiction of the HMRC level; it is not usable as a count without a scope/lag bridge.

RICS August 2026 is reported as -19/-17 (Sept-published survey, multiple outlets) in some copies and -18/-16 in the later September survey release; September is -22/-18. The differences are vintage/rounding, not different markets. Direction (mild deterioration in Sept, still far above the March low) is the usable content.

2026 annual forecasts: TwentyEA/TwentyCi cut to 1.13m from 1.2m (-6.8% vs 2025, +2.6% vs 2024); a separate forecast holds ~1.15m. Their scope is ambiguous (TwentyCi is described as England & Wales, and TwentyEA measures agreed sales), so they can constrain the monthly order of magnitude only through an explicit bridge factor, not as a count.

Structural turnover evidence disagrees by definition: ~5% of stock changing hands per year (Nationwide, recent), 1 transaction per 23 years = 4.3%/yr (2015 IMLA, based on a private-stock turnover series that fell from 12% to 4.5%). Applied to ~29m UK dwellings, 5% implies ~1.45m/yr and 4.3% implies ~1.26m/yr, the latter close to HMRC's recent ~1.15m/yr once the £40k threshold and the post-2015 decline in turnover are allowed for.

Cash share of transactions: ~40% of transactions (2026 commentary, two outlets) vs 58.3% of transaction VALUE funded by cash/equity in 2014. Different denominators (count vs value) and different years, so the 40% count share is the relevant one for grossing mortgage-financed completions up to all completions; the 2014 value share must not be substituted.

Long run of August SA values on the target definition (2017-2025) plus September 2025 gives the seasonal/monthly context and the year-on-year growth series; the August-to-September SA step has recently been slightly negative (2025: 97,040 to 95,980; 2024: 93,680 to ~92,290 implied by p41).

Sales-agreed volumes are down 6-9% YoY with four consecutive months of >5% decline, and the reported 5-6 month sales-agreed-to-completion lag (p28/p33/p139) plus the 2-4 month offer-to-completion lag (p15/p70/p71) mean these weak agreed sales mostly hit completions from late 2026 into 2027 - a downside tilt for September, but lagged enough that it must not be applied as a direct level.

Duplicate reporting of the same BoE approvals months; p175 (56,100 for July) conflicts with the BoE's 55,900 and appears to be a table column misread, so the BoE-stated 55,900 (p100) is the value carried forward.

methods.rationale: Primary own-history route on the exact target definition (HMRC UK residential, SA, monthly, £40k+), with one value per calendar month and the current vintage for each. It supplies last year's value for the target month (September 2025 = 95,980, p39) and recent months (June 98,390, July 96,650, August 95,220) from which the year-on-year growth of the last one to three months is taken: August was about -1.9% and July about -1.2% on the same basis, so September 2026 should land a little below 95,980 rather than at the August level. The older August values (2017-2024) provide the seasonal context of a slightly negative August-to-September SA step. Shared dependencies: everything here is one HMRC measurement; the main failure mode is that HMRC's 2026 seasonal factors behave unusually (the August 2026 SA/NSA ratio is ~0.99 versus ~0.92 a year earlier), so a level built from SA year-on-year growth is the safest use of this series. First-provisional versus settled vintage is a second-order issue: the July vintage moved only -0.06% (96,710 to 96,650), though September 2025 was revised up ~0.8% between releases.

p176.role: BoE net mortgage approvals for house purchase, UK, seasonally adjusted, June 2026 - first month of the 2-4 month lead window into September 2026 completions

p100.role: BoE net mortgage approvals for house purchase, UK, seasonally adjusted, July 2026 - middle month of the lead window

p99.role: BoE net mortgage approvals for house purchase, UK, seasonally adjusted, August 2026 - last month of the lead window

p81.role: Approximate share of UK residential transactions that are cash sales, used to gross mortgage-financed completions up to all completions

a1.role: Dimensionless conversion from net approvals to completed mortgaged purchases (lapses, porting, multi-month drawdown)

methods.rationale: Independent measurement route: BoE approvals lead HMRC completions by roughly 2-4 months (HMRC's own stated offer-to-completion lag), so September 2026 completions should track approvals centred on June-August 2026. That window averages 56,333, materially below the April level of 65,900, which is why this route sits below the summer run-rate. Grossing up by 1/(1-cash share) converts mortgage-financed completions to all transactions; a1 handles the residual approvals-to-completion mismatch. The formula is not circular with m1: its only target-series input is the cash-share point, which is a share of transactions, not the target level. Failure modes: the cash-share estimate comes from market commentary rather than a measured count, and if the true lag is closer to five or six months (as the sales-agreed-to-completion statements imply) then September should be supported by the higher March-May approvals and this route is biased low.

p446.role: UK total dwelling stock, approximately 29 million homes

p430.role: Average number of years between a UK home changing hands (one transaction per 23 years), the structural turnover denominator

a3.role: Dimensionless adjustment from the 2015 structural turnover norm to 2026 HMRC £40k+ UK completion levels

methods.rationale: Slow-moving structural baseline from capacity rather than momentum: stock divided by years-between-transactions converts to an annual transaction flow, and dividing by twelve gives a monthly norm; a3 brings the 2015 norm onto the current observed turnover level and covers the £40k threshold. It is generous to call this a forecast - it cannot see the 2026 cycle - but it is an independent anchor that keeps the estimate from drifting with a single month's noise. The structural evidence is internally inconsistent (5% of stock per year implies ~1.45m transactions, well above HMRC's ~1.15m), which is exactly why a3 is a downward adjustment with a wide range rather than a copied coefficient. Failure mode: if 2026 turnover has fallen further than a3 allows, this route is too high.

p345.role: TwentyEA revised forecast of UK residential property transactions for the whole of calendar 2026 (1.13 million)

a2.role: Dimensionless bridge from the forecast annual average monthly rate to the September 2026 seasonally adjusted HMRC level, covering scope (UK vs England & Wales, sales vs completions) and within-year seasonality

methods.rationale: Annual-total constraint: the mid-2026 forecast revision down from 1.2m to 1.13m captures expected momentum, and dividing by twelve gives a monthly level in the mid-90,000s that is broadly consistent with HMRC's April-August financial-year-to-date total (488,540 SA, ~97,700 a month) once the spring SDLT-driven spike is set aside. It is deliberately treated as a forecast, not an outcome: a2 is the bridge for scope (England & Wales versus UK, agreed sales versus completions) and for September's position within a year whose activity was front-loaded. Failure mode: if the forecast actually measures agreed sales, the completions level would typically be a little lower and this route is biased high.

assumptions.name: Conversion factor from net house-purchase mortgage approvals in the June-August 2026 lead window to completed mortgaged purchases counted by HMRC
assumptions.rationale: Approvals are net of cancellations and are dated at approval, whereas completions in a given month draw on approvals spread over several months and some mortgaged purchases (product transfers, porting, transfers between related parties) complete without a fresh house-purchase approval. Calibrating on the most recent observation, August 2026 SA completions of 95,220 against a June-August approvals mean of 56,333 implies total/approvals of about 1.69, versus 1/(1-0.40)=1.67 from the cash-share gross-up alone, so the residual conversion is close to 1. The range spans a lapse-heavy market (factor well below 1) and a chained-market month where completions draw on older, higher approvals (factor above 1).
assumptions.applies_when: The three-month approvals window is a reasonable summary of the 2-4 month offer-to-completion lag, and the ~40% cash share applies to transaction counts in 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that approvals-to-completion lapse rates rose sharply in 2026, or that the cash share of transaction counts is far from 40% (e.g. above 50% or below 30%).

assumptions.name: Bridge factor from the 2026 annual transactions forecast monthly average to the September 2026 seasonally adjusted HMRC level
assumptions.rationale: The TwentyEA/TwentyCi 1.13m forecast is described in one source as England & Wales and by TwentyEA's own measure of sales, while HMRC counts UK completions at £40k+; these scope differences could push either way. Within 2026 the March-April SDLT-related spike means the level is not flat across the year, and September has recently run slightly below the annual average. A near-unity bridge with a wide band is therefore used rather than a directional shift.
assumptions.applies_when: The forecast refers broadly to 2026 UK/E&W residential transactions at a comparable definition to HMRC completions, so that its monthly average is informative about September's order of magnitude.
assumptions.falsified_by: Clear evidence that the forecast counts sales agreed rather than completions, or that it excludes Scotland/Northern Ireland on a scale that shifts the UK total by more than ~10%.

assumptions.name: Adjustment of the 2015 structural turnover norm (one transaction per 23 years of dwelling stock) to 2026 UK £40k+ residential completions
assumptions.rationale: The 23-years-between-transactions figure comes from 2015 IMLA analysis, when private-stock turnover had already fallen from 12% to 4.5%; the Nationwide ~5% figure is a different, higher-frequency measure and would imply ~1.45m sales a year, well above HMRC's recent ~1.15m. HMRC 2025 completions of roughly 1.15m against ~29m dwellings imply about one transaction per 25 years, i.e. a factor near 0.9 on the 23-year norm; some of the gap is also the £40k threshold and non-dwelling/leasehold transfers. The range covers turnover recovering towards the 2015 norm and falling further.
assumptions.applies_when: The dwelling stock is around 29 million and current turnover is in the 3.8-4.6% range rather than the pre-crisis 8%.
assumptions.falsified_by: A measured 2026 turnover rate near the pre-crisis 8% or below 3.5%, or a materially different UK dwelling stock (e.g. above 31m).

The primary route ([[m1_weight]] weight) carries last year's September level of [[p39_value]] forward using recent year-on-year growth from [[p2_value]] and [[p1_value]]. Other routes anchor on mortgage approvals ([[p176_value]], [[p100_value]], [[p99_value]] with cash share [[p81_value]]), dwelling stock [[p446_value]] over [[p430_value]], and the annual forecast [[p345_value]]. Observed points are HMRC and BoE data; the conversion factors [[a1_value]], [[a2_value]] and [[a3_value]] are analyst assumptions, not observations. Blocks were combined by median with equal weight per block.

The main risk is that approvals have fallen sharply, so the momentum route may overstate completions. Better evidence would be September 2026 approvals and early completion counts.

Unit of the estimate: [[unit_full]].

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 Conversion factor from net house-purchase mortgage approvals in the June-August 2026 lead window to completed mortgaged purchases counted by HMRC: [[a1_value]] [n], range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]] (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that approvals-to-completion lapse rates rose sharply in 2026, or that the cash share of transaction counts is far from [n] (e.g. above [n] or below [n]).
- a2 Bridge factor from the 2026 annual transactions forecast monthly average to the September 2026 seasonally adjusted HMRC level: [[a2_value]] [n], range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]] (range widened by code); used by m4. - a3 Adjustment of the [n] structural turnover norm (one transaction per [n] years of dwelling stock) to 2026 UK £[n]k+ residential completions: [[a3_value]] [n], range [[a3_low]] to [[a3_high]] (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: A measured 2026 turnover rate near the pre-crisis [n] or below [n], or a materially different UK dwelling stock (e.g. above [n]m).

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 series_auto, yoy path: yoy2: last year's same month x the summed growth of the latest 2 year-on-year pairs. The best estimate for UK residential property transactions (£[n] or above), seasonally adjusted, in September 2026, as first provisionally reported by HMRC, is 94,166 transaction (80% model-based interval 65,585 to 135,204 transaction).

The primary route (50% weight) carries last year's September level of 95,980 transaction forward using recent year-on-year growth from 96,650 transaction and 95,220 transaction. Other routes anchor on mortgage approvals (58,200 transaction, 55,900 transaction, 54,900 transaction with cash share 40%), dwelling stock 29,000,000 dwelling over 23 years per transaction, and the annual forecast 1,130,000 transaction. Observed points are HMRC and BoE data; the conversion factors 1, 1 and 0.9 are analyst assumptions, not observations. Blocks were combined by median with equal weight per block.

The main risk is that approvals have fallen sharply, so the momentum route may overstate completions. Better evidence would be September 2026 approvals and early completion counts.

Unit of the estimate: transaction (total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 Conversion factor from net house-purchase mortgage approvals in the June-August 2026 lead window to completed mortgaged purchases counted by HMRC: 1 [n], range 0.7082 to 1.416 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that approvals-to-completion lapse rates rose sharply in 2026, or that the cash share of transaction counts is far from [n] (e.g. above [n] or below [n]).
- a2 Bridge factor from the 2026 annual transactions forecast monthly average to the September 2026 seasonally adjusted HMRC level: 1 [n], range 0.7001 to 1.4 (range widened by code); used by m4. Overturned by: Clear evidence that the forecast counts sales agreed rather than completions, or that it excludes Scotland/Northern Ireland on a scale that shifts the UK total by more than ~[n].
- a3 Adjustment of the [n] structural turnover norm (one transaction per [n] years of dwelling stock) to 2026 UK £[n]k+ residential completions: 0.9 [n], range 0.6307 to 1.261 (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: A measured 2026 turnover rate near the pre-crisis [n] or below [n], or a materially different UK dwelling stock (e.g. above [n]m).

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 series_auto, yoy path: yoy2: last year's same month x the summed growth of the latest 2 year-on-year pairs. by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
